newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel firm on tightness, shrugs off weak crude.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel firm on tightness, shrugs off weak crude.

text.p: The high sulphur cracked market was quiet, but the bullish tone was supported on Thursday by news Portugal had issued a tender to buy up to 150,000 tonnes for delivery in September, October and November.
Prices were assessed $1 up around $108-109 fob NWE although nothing was seen today in NWE and the market was still tight.

Activity in the barge market was essentially restricted to the morning when a high of $114.50 fob ARA was done. Tight supplies and lowering expectations of Russian straight run material landing in the barge market (several have now found homes) were supportive.
In the Med an ISAB high viscosity cargo was sold on Tuesday at high fob Med +$1.20.
Low sulphur cracked cargoes were also showing a steady tone, taking support from a perceived shortage of ready cargoes although a major was understood to have a cargo in the first decade of October.

Weaker crude futures were not pulling prices lower amid continued talk that a Turkish 50kt requirement had not been met. Prices were steady around $116-118 fob, still a little off swaps numbers of $118-119.
